correctness.rationale: Over a perfect algebraically closed field of characteristic 3, the Frobenius cube roots b_i^3=a_i yield the homogeneous normalization [S:T]→[S^3 T²:G_h(S,T):T⁵] with G_h^3=F_h(S³,T³). The morphism is finite birational since G(t)∉k(t³) (leading term t^5) and the field extension k(t)/k(t³) has prime degree 3, hence the normalization is P1. Finite singularities are exactly roots of F′(x)=2x⁴+a4x³+2a2x+a1. Since F″=2(x³+a2), only r³=−a2 may be repeated. For a1≠a4a2, F′ has four simple roots and four branches of semigroup <2,3>. On a1=a4a2, exact factorization F′=2(x−r)³(x−a4), giving multiplicities (3,1) and semigroups <3,4>+<2,3>, except when r=a4 (a2=−a4³), yielding multiplicity four and semigroup <3,5>. Infinity has <2,5>, delta2 throughout; finite delta sum4 so total delta6 equals quintic arithmetic genus6. Local t-expansions give leading orders 2/4/5 after removal of t³ terms, coprime to 3. Frobenius is bijective on every finite extension, so normalized P1→X induces one rational preimage per rational singular or smooth point, giving q^n+1 and zeta of P1. Independent exact checks covered all 243 monic F3 quintics, giving derivative patterns 162/54/27 (squarefree subset 120/24/18), and verified F3/F9 point counts.

value.rationale: Characteristic three is exactly the degree of the cyclic trigonal cover and therefore a distinguished bad characteristic of the canonical genus-four family. The jump from four A2-like cusps to (3,4)+(2,3) to (3,5), with delta conservation and rational normalization, is a complete natural collision/boundary classification under explicit coefficient equations. It is more than a normalization observation or arbitrary low-degree numerical example, and the associated exact zeta identity clarifies arithmetic degeneration. The theorem deliberately avoids claims of stable reduction or Jacobian specialization.
